sections.subtitle: Match context
sections.text: A London derby at Brentford Community Stadium. Brentford are 7th (47 points) and Fulham are 12th (44). The Sofascore model gives Brentford a 52% chance, draw 24%, Fulham 24%, with a 55% chance of both teams to score.

sections.subtitle: Current form
sections.text: Brentford have drawn 4 in a row and are unbeaten in 3, often carrying the expected goals edge (2.56–1.33 v Wolverhampton; 2.84–1.53 v Everton). Fulham are 1-1-3 across 5, creating well in their 3-1 win v Burnley (expected goals 3.15) but failing to score in 3 of those matches.

sections.subtitle: Head-to-head
sections.text: Fulham won the last 2 meetings (3-2 away, 3-1 home). Recent clashes tend to be open: more than 2.5 goals in 8/9 and both teams scoring in 6/8. Harry Wilson has been a standout against Brentford (4 goals, average rating 7.56).

sections.subtitle: Season stats snapshot
sections.text: Brentford are elite chance creators (98 big chances, league rank 1) and strike late (16 goals after 76'). Their finishing can be erratic (56 big chances missed), but Igor Thiago is reliable (21 league goals). Fulham sit mid-table (43 scored, 46 conceded) on 44 points.

sections.subtitle: Tactical notes and key players
sections.text: Brentford’s direct breaks and crossing supply regular opportunities (9 headed goals; accurate crosses rank 6). Dango Ouattara’s service (11 big chances created) and Thiago’s movement should trouble a Fulham defence that have recently allowed several big chances. For Fulham, Wilson’s form (2 goals, 2 assists last 5) and delivery support Raul Jimenez, though he is under expected goals this season.

sections.subtitle: Referee, cards and corners
sections.text: Paul Tierney averages 3.3 yellows and 0.12 reds per match. Brentford home games lean lower on cards, while Fulham away have trended higher; expect a moderate count. Fulham’s recent fixtures have brought high corner volumes, with Brentford lower at home; expect around average to slightly above-average totals.

sections.subtitle: Match prediction
sections.text: Brentford’s chance creation and home edge point their way, but Fulham’s recent head-to-head record and Wilson’s threat keep it competitive. With the model leaning home and both teams to score slightly favoured, a narrow Brentford win is the likeliest outcome.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Match context
halftimeSections.text: Goalless at the break at Brentford Community Stadium, but the home side have created the clearer chance. Possession has leaned Fulham’s way, yet Brentford’s direct play and set-piece threat have produced the best opening. The game state remains finely balanced and one moment of quality or a set piece could decide it.

halftimeSections.subtitle: First-half summary
halftimeSections.text: Numbers edge towards Brentford for chance quality: expected goals 0.39-0.23, big chances 1-0, shots on target 1-0. Territory is close: final-third entries 25-19, penalty-area entries 12-11. Fulham have had more of the ball (40-60) but little end product. Duels have favoured Brentford (53%-47%). Corners 4-2 to Brentford. Discipline: Brentford 0 yellows, Fulham 1 yellow (Sasa Lukic).

halftimeSections.subtitle: Attack momentum
halftimeSections.text: Brentford started strongly with sustained pressure across the opening 20 minutes. Fulham then enjoyed a prolonged spell from around 21 to 37 minutes, pinning Brentford deeper without clear shots on target. The half finished with Brentford back on the front foot, including a late surge just before the interval.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Tactical notes
halftimeSections.text: Brentford’s most effective route has been early service into Igor Thiago and quick combinations around Mathias Jensen, who has supplied 1 big chance and 3 key passes. More first-time crosses and second-ball pressure can increase the volume of good looks. Fulham’s possession has been neat but too safe; quicker vertical passes into Rodrigo Muniz and earlier releases to Alex Iwobi and Harry Wilson could open lanes. With Sasa Lukic on a booking, Fulham must manage midfield duels carefully to avoid exposing the back line in transitions.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Referee, cards and corners
halftimeSections.text: First half: cards 1 (Fulham), corners 4-2 (Brentford). Projection: a tight second half with 2-3 additional cards, with Fulham’s midfield the main risk zone. Corners likely to remain close but Brentford can retain a narrow edge given their crossing volume from open play and set pieces, pointing towards a total around 9-11.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Second-half outlook
halftimeSections.text: The next 15 minutes should suit Brentford’s direct pressure and set pieces. Fulham’s control of possession keeps them in the contest, but they must turn entries into shots. Given the first-half patterns and chance quality, the edge for the first goal leans towards Brentford, with a low-scoring outcome most likely.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Match prediction
halftimeSections.text: Brentford to strike first after the break, with Igor Thiago the most likely scorer from open play or a recycled set piece. Forecast: Brentford 1-0 Fulham, with a low total after the interval.
